summary:
Radar for 2026-11-14 (ObesityWeek runs 14–17 Nov). There are three time-sensitive openings.

1. **Stopping tirzepatide is getting a fresh news hook.** On 15 Nov Cleveland Clinic presents a study comparing 5 strategies after people stop. Fox ("6 rebound risks"), Yahoo ("hit my goal weight, what now?") and Medical Daily (an analysis not yet reviewed by other scientists) are already covering stopping. This fits our broad "Stopping" long-form, which has a 6.35% click-through rate. Use it for a refreshed long-form and a ▶ Watch next link.
2. **Nature Metabolism study, 13 Nov.** Rare variants in the GLP-1 receptor gene went with much less weight loss on semaglutide (2.4% vs 8.9%) but not on tirzepatide (13.3% vs 15.2%). It's a strong "why didn't it work for me?" hook, but each group has under 20 people and it's observational. Treat it as an emerging Short, with no switching advice.
3. **The FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning is a label change, and the AAO, MedPage and The Hill are still writing about it.** About 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 people per year in the FDA's pooled trials. It fits the label-change format.

**Watch tomorrow (15 Nov):**
- EloraTZP Phase 2 in obesity plus type 2 diabetes. Lilly's release names no tirzepatide-only comparison yet. If the full data shows a randomized tirzepatide-alone arm, it becomes the fast-turn "Did X beat tirzepatide?" format that earned 44% of our watch time.
- SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS.
- Retatrutide sleep apnea (TRIUMPH-1 and -2).

**Ongoing:**
- Thanksgiving and fullness Shorts start 18 Nov.
- Evergreen formats: first-month timeline, Zepbound KwikPen how-to (Instructions for Use only), and felt-symptom Shorts (hair, nausea, burping, injection site).

**Rejected:** compounded or "cheapest tirzepatide" listicles, and Rogan/peptide-market retatrutide talk.

**Skipped:** cost and coverage stories (CVS, Deloitte, Wegovy pill price), which are banned.

**Sources checked:**
- [Cleveland Clinic newsroom](https://newsroom.clevelandclinic.org/2026/11/14/cleveland-clinic-study-identifies-best-treatment-strategies-for-weight-loss-after-stopping-glp-1-drugs)
- [Nature Metabolism](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42255-026-01661-2)
- [Pharmacy Times NAION](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/fda-requires-class-wide-glp-1-ra-labeling-changes-for-potential-naion-risk)
- [Lilly ObesityWeek release](https://investor.lilly.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lilly-present-new-data-across-zepbound-foundayo-eloratzp-and)
- [Stocktitan summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/LLY/lilly-to-present-new-data-across-zepbound-foundayo-elora-tzp-and-3wdn6ju8hlkp.html)
- [REDEFINE 4 (Healio)](https://www.healio.com/news/endocrinology/20260414/zepbound-bests-cagrisema-for-weight-loss-among-adults-with-obesity)
- [KwikPen launch (PharmTech)](https://www.pharmtech.com/view/eli-lilly-introduces-multi-dose-zepbound-kwikpen-to-expand-obesity-treatment-options)
- [Danish pregnancy study (SciTechDaily)](https://scitechdaily.com/study-of-750000-pregnancies-challenges-fears-over-popular-weight-loss-drugs/)

candidates.topic: Stopping tirzepatide: what happens next, refreshed by Cleveland Clinic's ObesityWeek study comparing 5 strategies after stopping semaglutide or tirzepatide (presented 15 Nov), plus SURMOUNT-4
candidates.angle: Broad long-form: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) After Stopping: What Studies Show'. Start with SURMOUNT-4: 335 vs 335 people; those switched to placebo regained 14.0%, yet still ended 9.9% below their starting weight. Then the real-world Cleveland Clinic data: people who stopped with no further obesity treatment had the smallest average weight loss at 2 years (about 4%). It's observational, and it shows how much having a plan with your clinician matters. Give no stopping or switching advice. Say 'talk to your prescriber before any change'. Don't push surgery; mention it as one strategy the study looked at, and no more.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (ObesityWeek coverage 15–17 Nov, then New Year 'what now' searches)
candidates.why_now: Cleveland Clinic newsroom release on 14 Nov for a 15 Nov ObesityWeek talk. Fox News ('6 rebound risks'), Yahoo ('I hit my goal weight — what now?') and Medical Daily (an analysis not yet reviewed by other scientists) are all covering stopping this week. Our Stopping long-form is our best recent broad video (309 min, 6.35% CTR). This topic has appeared in 4+ of our snapshots.

evidence.signal: 5-strategy comparison after stopping GLP-1s. Stopping with no further treatment had the smallest average loss (4%) at 2 years.
'Ozempic and Zepbound users face 6 rebound risks after stopping' (12 Nov)
7,938 patients. In the obesity group, 55% regained after stopping and 45% held or kept losing; many restarted or switched.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your eyes: the FDA's new class-wide NAION warning, explained from the label
candidates.angle: Label change explained, calm and specific. What NAION is. The FDA's meta-analysis of 126 RCTs: about 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 person-years (GLP-1 vs comparator). It's rare. The symptom to act on: sudden, painless vision loss or blurring in one eye, often on waking, means contact a clinician right away. Then the scoped don't-stop-on-your-own line. Name both NANOS and the AAO only if they're quoted.
candidates.why_now: The FDA ordered the class labelling change on 9 Nov. Coverage is still going: AAO explainer (11 Nov), NeurologyLive and MedPage (13 Nov), The Hill op-ed, Blavity (14 Nov). The label-change format beats our usual views by 10x+ in this niche. Fox local stations are running 'What is NAION?' explainers.

evidence.signal: FDA requires class-wide NAION labelling for GLP-1 RAs
FDA orders vision-loss warnings added to Warnings and Precautions
Mainstream 'What is NAION?' explainer: the general public is searching

candidates.topic: Why semaglutide may not work for some people but tirzepatide did: rare GLP1R gene variants (Nature Metabolism, 13 Nov)
candidates.angle: Tirzepatide-first 'what's confirmed?' Short for the 13:00 slot. In people carrying rare damaging variants of the GLP-1 receptor gene, semaglutide weight loss was 2.4% (n=17) vs 8.9% in matched controls. On tirzepatide it was 13.3% vs 15.2% (n=19). The likely reason: tirzepatide also acts on the GIP receptor. These variants are rare, the groups are tiny, and it's observational genetics. It doesn't explain most slow responses, and you can't test for it at the pharmacy. Give no switching advice: 'if you're not responding, talk to your prescriber'.
keywords: why ozempic didn't work for me
candidates.why_now: Published 13 Nov in Nature Metabolism, with a companion paper. So far only Bioengineer.org and Google News have picked it up, and there's almost no creator coverage. 'Ozempic stopped working, switched to Mounjaro' is a huge Reddit theme, and BBC Science Focus ran 'Why weight-loss drugs stop working for some people' on 14 Nov.

evidence.signal: Rare GLP1R variants diminish weight loss on semaglutide but not on tirzepatide
A second paper finds the same weaker response to semaglutide but not tirzepatide
A common GLP1R variant adds about 0.76 kg per copy; a GIPR variant predicts vomiting on tirzepatide only. Useful context.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) first month: what to expect week by week, from the label and trials
candidates.angle: Broad what-to-expect long-form, top of the playbook's priority list. Cover appetite and food noise; GI effects that happened 'mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time'; injection-site reactions (6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo); hydration; and which signs mean calling your prescriber. No dosing or titration instructions. Second concrete payoff at 15–30 s.
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady; spikes with New Year starts (late Dec to Jan)
candidates.why_now: Top of the performance playbook's priority list; How Long added +31 min today. The new-starter wave grows into January, and celebrity coverage (DJ Khaled's Wegovy story, 12–14 Nov) drives first-timer searches.

evidence.signal: Label and trial basis for GI timing and injection-site rates
The DJ Khaled Wegovy story is lifting mainstream curiosity among new starters

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: full after 3 bites, protein first, eating slower, and easing nausea at a big meal
candidates.angle: Holiday-fullness Shorts from 18 Nov, the 20:00 funnel slot pointing to the Thanksgiving long-form. Calm and practical, with no extreme-diet messaging. Don't say slower stomach emptying 'causes' anything; use the label wording.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea: why it happens, when it usually eases, and what helps
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom 'Is this normal?' Short. Label wording: GI effects happened mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time. Practical help: smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping when full, going easy on greasy food. Name the emergency trigger (severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting) and keep 'right away'.
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady; holiday meals lift it from 20 Nov
candidates.why_now: Felt-symptom searches beat our usual views by 10x+. Our nausea Short got 183 views (above the median), and a GIPR-variant/vomiting genetics angle adds a fresh fact.

evidence.signal: A GIPR variant was linked to vomiting on tirzepatide, not semaglutide. A fresh fact for a nausea Short.

candidates.topic: Lifting weights on tirzepatide: T-REx randomized trial (Nature Medicine, 9 Nov). Less lean-mass loss, and strength up instead of down
candidates.angle: Short (and a fresh chapter or Watch-next for the Strength long-form). 120 men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70 with obesity. Three resistance sessions a week went with about 25% less lean-mass loss than tirzepatide alone, and strength rose about 10% instead of falling about 10%. Give the exact population and arms; no 'everyone loses muscle' fear.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical (12 Nov) and Korean press (14 Nov) picked it up, MindBodyGreen has a muscle-on-GLP-1 piece, and the Lancet COURAGE muscle-preservation trial landed on 11 Nov. It's a fresh RCT, and few creators have covered it so far.

evidence.signal: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy: RCT
'Muscle benefits of lifting weights while taking tirzepatide' (12 Nov)

candidates.topic: EloraTZP Phase 2 in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (ObesityWeek, 15 Nov). Watch for a tirzepatide-alone comparison
candidates.angle: Our best-earning format, if it qualifies. Lilly's release reports up to 23.3% average weight loss at 48 weeks and up to 2.9% A1C reduction in adults with obesity or overweight plus type 2 diabetes, but names no tirzepatide-alone arm. If the full presentation shows a randomized comparison against tirzepatide alone, fast-turn 'Did EloraTZP beat tirzepatide?' within 48 h and link it to the 10-01 EloraTZP video. If it doesn't, do one 13:00 Short only. It's investigational, so it 'isn't approved'.
candidates.why_now: Presented 15 Nov, 3:30 pm ET. The 'eloralintide' and 'eloratzp' searches drove 44% of our long-form minutes, so the audience is already searching for this drug.

evidence.signal: EloraTZP Phase 2 obesity + T2D data at ObesityWeek
Up to 23.3% at 48 weeks; A1C down up to 2.9%; no head-to-head named

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide: which works better? The approved head-to-head (SURMOUNT-5), with REDEFINE 4 and the new GLP1R-variant data as context
candidates.angle: Approved-drug head-to-head long-form (search-demand format). Use SURMOUNT-5 in adults with obesity without diabetes for the main result. Add CagriSema vs tirzepatide (REDEFINE 4: 23.0% vs 25.5% at 84 weeks, open-label, 809 adults with obesity; non-inferiority not met) as a separate trial, not a cross-trial comparison. Close on 'which is right for you is a prescriber conversation'.
keywords: zepbound vs wegovy which is better

candidates.why_now: Evergreen top search in the niche; the 13 Nov genetics paper and ObesityWeek give a fresh hook. EloraTZP showed head-to-heads drive our watch time.

evidence.signal: Zepbound bests CagriSema in REDEFINE 4 (adults with obesity)
Fresh difference between semaglutide and tirzepatide

Never state amounts or doses. Cite the real IFU URL (not the PI). It complements the 11-11 Pen video (single-dose pen) and points viewers to it.

candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Short or a chapter. The label lists burping (eructation) and GERD. Practical tips: smaller meals, not lying down right after eating, going easy on greasy food. Never say slower stomach emptying 'causes' it. Call your prescriber if heartburn is severe or persistent.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and sleep apnea: TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-2 Phase 3 (ObesityWeek, 15 Nov)
candidates.angle: 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short. Breathing disruptions (AHI) fell by up to an average of 60.6% (TRIUMPH-1: moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity or overweight) and 48.1% (TRIUMPH-2: also type 2 diabetes) at 80 weeks. 'Up to' means the top dose. Retatrutide isn't approved. Close with tirzepatide context: it's already approved for OSA in adults with obesity, per the Zepbound label.
candidates.why_now: Presented 15 Nov at ObesityWeek. Retatrutide interest is high (GoodRx side-effects and mechanism pieces on 13 Nov, Rogan mentions). Only a Short: no pipeline long-form explainers.

evidence.signal: Up to 60.6% and 48.1% AHI reductions at 80 weeks
ObesityWeek schedule, 15 Nov

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide in teens: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (21.4% average BMI reduction at 72 weeks), as England reports hundreds of children on weight-loss jabs
candidates.angle: For parents in our audience: a 'what's confirmed?' Short. Average BMI fell 21.4% in 12- to under-18-year-olds with obesity, and more than half no longer met the obesity BMI cut-off. Check the current approval status before scripting; avoid 'approved yet?' framing. No body-shaming and no before/after.
candidates.why_now: Presented 15 Nov. The Guardian (14 Nov) reported hundreds of children in England prescribed weight-loss jabs. It falls outside our core adult audience, so it's lower fit.

evidence.signal: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS: 21.4% BMI reduction at 72 weeks
Hundreds of children in England prescribed weight-loss jabs (14 Nov)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines around pregnancy: Danish study of 750,000+ pregnancies found no preterm-birth link with weight-loss use, but higher odds with use for diabetes
candidates.angle: Class-level Short ('GLP-1 medicines', since the data are semaglutide and liraglutide, not tirzepatide). The pattern differed by why people were prescribed the medicine; diabetes itself may explain part of it. It's observational registry data. Pair it with the tirzepatide label's pregnancy and birth-control points, with no stopping advice.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily (13 Nov) and Medical Daily (14 Nov) picked it up, following the 'Ozempic baby' NPR story. But our Birth Control long-form earned only 7 min, so keep it to a Short.

evidence.signal: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
No preterm link for weight-loss use; higher with diabetes use (liraglutide +70%, semaglutide +84%)

candidates.angle: Refresh hook for the Food Noise long-form via a Short. Patient-reported, real-world and company-sponsored data, so the wording must be 'linked to' or 'reported'. The title must name the drug the evidence covers (semaglutide or eloralintide), not tirzepatide.
